{
  "target_material": "Ti",
  "process_type": "plasma-enhanced ALD",
  "main_precursors": ["TiCl4", "atomic H"],
  "temperature_range": "20 to 200 °C",
  "summary": "The study investigates the growth kinetics and initial stage growth during plasma-enhanced Ti atomic layer deposition (PE-ALD). The process uses TiCl4 as a source gas and atomic H generated by rf plasma as the reducing agent. The growth rate is influenced by parameters such as TiCl4 exposure time, H exposure time, rf plasma power, and sample temperature. The growth kinetics are modeled to predict growth rates based on key parameters, and the effect of different substrate materials on initial growth rates is analyzed.",
  "evidence": "Ti ALD films were grown at temperatures from 20 to 200 °C using TiCl4 as a source gas and rf plasma-produced atomic H as the reducing agent. The growth rates were independent of TiCl4 exposure above 13103 L, indicating typical ALD mode growth. The growth kinetics were modeled to predict the growth rates based upon these results. The initial growth rates on Pt, Al, Au, and Cu are higher due to the higher Cl extraction rates, while those on Si and amorphous C are smaller due to etching of substrate materials by atomic H."
}
